solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Next, I'm to act as arbitrator

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
to mediate is to act as a go-between or arbitrator in a dispute

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are the next person to step in and settle a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate can mean nearest or directly following, as in your immediate neighbour, so it is a synonym of next.

clue.text: Move slowly and gradually in church

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church; that the letters also run unbroken across 'in church' is a coincidence of this charade

explanation.surface: A procession creeps step by step through a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is a verb meaning to advance by tiny amounts, one small distance at a time.

clue.text: Mike with ammunition tailed the huge animal once

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ammo is the short informal word for ammunition

indicators.note: tailed here means docked of its tail, so the word the loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A hunter named Mike, armed with ammunition, follows the trail of a giant prehistoric beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The woolly mammoth was a huge elephant-like creature now extinct, which is why the clue says once.

clue.text: Couple united during party

indicators.note: during means the letter goes within the party word, inside it in time and so in space

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or celebration
U is the usual abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A couple is joined together in marriage in the middle of a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair of people, especially performers, so it means a couple.

clue.text: Painter is tucking into baked tart

indicators.note: tucking into means the word is goes inside the other letters, like a diner eating
baked suggests the word tart has been cooked and changed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter takes a break from the canvas to eat a freshly baked tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baked' looks like it describes the tart, but it is the signal to rearrange those letters before 'is' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist is someone who creates pictures, and a painter is the classic example.

clue.text: US writer's pen found under Old Testament book

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means this piece comes below the other in the grid

parts.note: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament
a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen

explanation.surface: A literary scholar finds an American author's pen tucked beneath a Bible open at an Old Testament book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool to go with the writer, but it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was an American modernist poet, author of The Cantos, so he is a US writer.

clue.text: Feel sick if beer is spoken of?

indicators.note: spoken of says the beer word is heard rather than written, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether merely talking about beer will make them unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is an old-fashioned verb meaning to be unwell or in poor health.

clue.text: In the morning, is drop of spirits wrong?

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

indicators.note: a drop of something is a tiny amount, here just the opening letter of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a nip of whisky before noon is a bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means faulty or not as it should be, as in something is amiss.

clue.text: Extra large organ displayed around Great Britain

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: displayed around means the organ word is spread out round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: the eye is an organ of sight

explanation.surface: A huge body part is put on show all over Britain as a bonus attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an extra is a run not credited to the batsman; a leg bye is one scored after the ball hits the batsman's body.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg bye is one of the kinds of extra run in cricket, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Fertiliser's price restricting old representative

indicators.note: restricting means the price word hems in the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: cost is a synonym of price
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A gardener grumbles that the price of fertiliser is keeping out an elderly politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Compost is decayed plant matter dug into soil to enrich it, a natural fertiliser.

clue.text: Regretting game in capital of Ghana

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: capital means the opening letter, the capital letter, of Ghana

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry about a match played in Accra, Ghana's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Ghana' tempts you toward Accra; it only means the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing is the present participle of rue, to feel sorrow or remorse about something.

clue.text: Charlie cooked Ron his unhealthy-looking pie

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: cooked suggests the words have been mixed and transformed, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: pasty means pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: Charlie cooked a pie for Ron that looked pallid and unappetising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges RONHIS to ORNISH. A Cornish pasty is a pastry from Cornwall, in south-west England, filled with beef and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish pasty is a folded pastry case with a savoury filling, a kind of pie.

clue.text: Fruit in tree can corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fruit growing on a tree may go rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a stone fruit.

clue.text: Elegant and stylish hotel secured by commander in chief

indicators.note: secured by means the hotel letter is held fast inside the commander's letters

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A smart, fashionable hotel has been taken over by the head of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic describes something fashionable with sophisticated good taste.

clue.text: Bone in Dublin Bay occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of Dublin Bay is taken

explanation.surface: Every now and then a bone washes up in Dublin Bay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm.

clue.text: Northern university to remove sort of waste that's harmful

parts.note: to clear something is to remove it, as in clearing debris

explanation.surface: A university in the north of England is told to get rid of dangerous rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear waste is radioactive material from reactors, hazardous for thousands of years.

clue.text: Five beset by crazed zombies endlessly — in this type of film?

indicators.note: beset by means the five letter is surrounded on all sides by the other letters
crazed means driven wild, so the letters are jumbled
endlessly means zombies loses both of its end letters

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people are surrounded by mad zombies, which is exactly what happens in a cheap horror flick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims ZOMBIES to OMBIE, 'crazed' rearranges that to BMOIE, and 'beset by' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A B-movie is a low-budget picture, originally the supporting feature, and zombie horror is a staple of the genre.

clue.text: Crew that rows hard placing in the top ten

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat rowed by eight oarsmen, and its crew
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A rowing crew pulls hard and finishes in the leading group of a regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighth is a finishing position, and coming eighth still puts you within the first ten.

clue.text: Fellow bold, briefly, to dip in water seeing exotic aquatic bird

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: daring means bold or adventurous
to duck someone is to plunge them briefly under water

explanation.surface: A brave man ducks into the water on spotting a colourful foreign bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandarin duck is a brightly patterned waterfowl native to East Asia.

clue.text: Bottle: some Pilsener verified

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bottle of lager is checked and confirmed to be genuine Pilsener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like the container for the beer, but it is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, bottle means courage, as in losing your bottle, so it is a synonym of nerve.

clue.text: Greek character joins learner and other people

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A Greek man teams up with a trainee and some others.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al is the Latin abbreviation used in citations to mean together with others.

clue.text: Recklessly drive Maestro from Italy?

indicators.note: reckless driving is wild and erratic, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: An Italian conductor is told to drive dangerously.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian opera composer; the question mark admits he is one example of a maestro.

clue.text: Husband with books to sample, most current

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books
to test something is to sample or try it

explanation.surface: A husband with a pile of books tries out the latest titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot means up-to-the-minute or fashionable, so the hottest thing is the newest and most topical.

clue.text: Not entirely silent upset stomach

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, so in a down clue the letters read upwards
not entirely means the word is incomplete, missing its final letter

parts.note: mute means silent

explanation.surface: Someone suffering a quiet bout of indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' cuts MUTE to MUT, and 'upset' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tum is a childish or informal word for the stomach or belly.

clue.text: Remove coat of newer sheep

indicators.note: removing the coat strips the outside, so the first and last letters of newer go, like shearing

explanation.surface: Instructions to shear the fleece off a younger sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewe is the farming term for an adult female of the flock, so it names one kind of sheep by example.

clue.text: Short-lived English public house largely green

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: largely means most of the word but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: emerald is a bright green colour

explanation.surface: A pub in England painted mostly green has not lasted long.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral describes things that last only a very brief time, such as mayflies.
